```{r load-lib, message = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(tidymodels)


```

## Import and check the data
```{r load-data}
# Use simple column names because the original temperature headers contain degree symbols.
bikes <- read_csv(
  "data/SeoulBikeData.csv",
  skip = 1,
  col_names = c(
    "date", "rentals", "hour", "temperature_c", "humidity_pct",
    "wind_speed_ms", "visibility_10m", "dew_point_c", "solar_radiation",
    "rainfall_mm", "snowfall_cm", "season", "holiday", "functioning"
  ),
  col_types = cols(date = col_date(format = "%d/%m/%Y"))
)

glimpse(bikes)
summarise(bikes, first_date = min(date), last_date = max(date))
count(bikes, functioning)
```

## Classify working and non-working days

```{r prepare-day-type}
# Compare hours when the bike service was operating.
bikes_open <- bikes %>%
  filter(functioning == "Yes") %>%
  mutate(
    weekday = wday(date),
    # Public holidays belong to the non-working group even when they fall on a weekday.
    day_type = if_else(
      weekday == 1 | weekday == 7 | holiday == "Holiday",
      "Non-working day",
      "Working day"
    )
  )

count(bikes_open, day_type)
```

## Calculate mean hourly rentals

```{r summarise-hourly-rentals}
# Keep the sample size because the two day types contain different numbers of observations.
hourly_rentals <- bikes_open %>%
  group_by(season, day_type, hour) %>%
  summarise(
    n_hours = n(),
    mean_rentals = mean(rentals)
  )

# Check one point on each autumn curve before plotting.
filter(hourly_rentals, season == "Autumn", hour == 8)
```

## Compare hourly rental patterns across seasons

```{r plot-hourly-rentals}
# Use the same vertical scale in all four panels so rental levels can be compared across seasons.
ggplot(
  data = hourly_rentals,
  mapping = aes(x = hour, y = mean_rentals, colour = day_type)
) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ season, ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    x = "Hour of day",
    y = "Mean rentals per hour",
    colour = "Day type"
  )
```
## Identify the peak rental hour for each curve

```{r identify-peak-hours}
# Compare all 24 hourly means within each season and day type.
peak_hours <- hourly_rentals %>%
  group_by(season, day_type) %>%
  filter(mean_rentals == max(mean_rentals)) %>%
  select(season, day_type, hour, mean_rentals)

peak_hours
```
## Compare working and non-working days at the same hour

```{r compare-same-hour}
hourly_gaps <- hourly_rentals %>%
  # Leave out n_hours so that the two day types line up by season and hour.
  select(season, hour, day_type, mean_rentals) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = day_type, values_from = mean_rentals) %>%
  # A positive gap means more rentals on working days.
  mutate(gap = `Working day` - `Non-working day`)

# Compare the morning and afternoon gaps in autumn.
filter(hourly_gaps, season == "Autumn", hour == 8 | hour == 15)
hourly_gaps %>%
  group_by(season) %>%
  filter(gap == max(gap))
```
## Does the working-day gap at 08:00 vary by season?

```{r model-morning-rentals}
# Keep one 08:00 observation per operating date so the model retains day-to-day variation.
morning <- bikes_open %>%
  filter(hour == 8)

# Allow rental levels to vary by season, with one common working-day gap.
common_gap <- linear_reg() %>%
  set_engine("lm") %>%
  fit(rentals ~ season + day_type, data = morning)

# Allow the working-day gap itself to vary by season.
seasonal_gap <- linear_reg() %>%
  set_engine("lm") %>%
  fit(rentals ~ season * day_type, data = morning)

glance(common_gap)$adj.r.squared
glance(seasonal_gap)$adj.r.squared
```

## Check the residuals of the 08:00 model

```{r check-morning-residuals}
# Compare each morning's observed rentals with the fitted value for its group.
morning_check <- morning %>%
  bind_cols(predict(seasonal_gap, morning)) %>%
  mutate(residual = rentals - .pred)

# Use the same vertical scale across seasons to compare the spread of the residuals.
ggplot(morning_check, aes(x = day_type, y = residual)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(~ season, ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    x = "Day type",
    y = "Observed minus fitted rentals at 08:00"
  )
morning_check %>%
  group_by(season, day_type) %>%
  summarise(residual_sd = sd(residual))
```
